segnis: segnis, -e — slow, sluggish, idle (m./f. nom. sg.)
servare: servō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to keep, watch, observe, preserve (pres. inf.)
sibi: suī (reflexive pron.) — to/for himself, herself, themselves (dat.)
signa: signum, -ī (n.) — sign, portent, token (acc. pl.) · also nom. pl.
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sistit: sistō, -ere, stitī, statum — to set, place, make stand; stand (3rd sg. pres.)
solvitur: solvō, -ere, solvī, solūtum — to loose, release, dissolve; pass. be released, relax (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
speculatus: speculor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to spy out, watch, observe (dep.; perf. part., m. nom. sg.)
squalentem: squāleō, squālēre — to be rough, caked, unkempt; squalentem, matted (pres. part., f. acc. sg.)
stant: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm (3rd pl. pres.)
statione: statiō, -ōnis (f.) — post, station, guard duty (abl. sg.)
sternit: sternō, sternere, strāvī, strātum — to lay low, strew, spread (3rd sg. pres.)
stipata: stīpō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to press together, crowd round, throng (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
subit: subeō, subīre, subiī, subitum — to go under, approach, enter (3rd sg. pres.)
subito: subitō (adv.) — suddenly; also subitus, -a, -um, sudden (abl./dat. sg.)
suprema: suprēmus, -a, -um — highest, last, extreme (superl. of superus; f. nom./abl. sg.; n. pl.)
tali: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (m./f./n. abl. sg.; n. dat. sg.)
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
tarchon: Tarchōn, -onis (m.) — Tarchon, Etruscan leader and ally of Aeneas (nom. sg.)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
tellure: tellūs, tellūris (f.) — earth, ground, land (abl. sg.)
tendunt: tendō, tendere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, strain; to head for, make toward (3rd pl. pres.)
tenent: teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, restrain (3rd pl. pres.)
terra: terra, -ae (f.) — land, earth, ground (nom./abl. sg.) · also f. voc. sg. (ō terra hospita)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
tollit: tollō, tollere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, raise (3rd sg. pres.)
tollite: tollō, -ere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, take up (pl. imper.)
tollunt: tollō, -ere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, raise; se tollere, to rise up (3rd pl. pres.)
traiecto: trāiciō, -ere, -iēcī, -iectum — to throw across, pass across (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. sg.)
transtra: trānstrum, -ī (n.) — cross-beam, thwart, rower's bench (acc./nom. pl.)
trepidi: trepidus, -a, -um — alarmed, anxious, in haste (m. nom. pl.; gen. sg.)
tres: trēs, tria — three (m. nom. pl., as noun: three men) · also f. nom. pl. (trēs … turmae)
tris: trēs, tria — three (m./f. acc. pl., = trēs)
troianae: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan (f. gen./dat. sg.; nom. pl.)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turmas: turma, -ae (f.) — troop, squadron, cavalry troop (acc. pl.)
turno: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli (dat. sg., Turnō, 'to Turnus'; also abl. sg.)
turnum: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutulians, rival of Aeneas for Lavinia (acc. sg.)
ullum: ullus, -a, -um — any (n. nom./acc. sg.; also m. acc. sg.)
ultro: ultrō (adv.) — of one's own accord, voluntarily; besides
usque: usque (adv.) — all the way, continuously, ever, without ceasing
validis: validus, -a, -um — strong, powerful, stout (m./n. abl./dat. pl.)
varios: varius, -a, -um — various, diverse, changing (m. acc. pl.)
vel: vel (conj., adv.) — or; even; vel… vel, either… or
venientis: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (pres. part., f. gen. sg., with fāmae)
venti: ventus, -ī (m.) — wind (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl., in address (sine nūmine, ventī)
venus: Venus, Veneris (f.) — Venus, goddess of love, mother of Aeneas (nom. sg.)
versat: versō, -āre — to turn over, ponder (3rd sg. pres.)
vir: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. sg.)
viribus: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, strength; pl. vīrēs, vīrium, strength (abl./dat. pl.)
viro: vir, virī (m.) — man (dat. sg.) · also abl. sg. (proque virō, in place of the man)
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
vocem: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, sound (acc. sg.)
voces: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, utterance (acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)
volans: volō, -āre — to fly (pres. part., m. nom. sg.) · also f. nom. sg. (columba volāns)
vomit: vomō, -ere, -uī, -itum — to vomit, spew forth, pour out (3rd sg. pres. ind. act.)
